# Backtest with covariates (1946-2025), cutoffs 1960-2014

<!-- Generated by `python -m forecast.backtest --out docs/backtests/2026-10-logit-covariates.md` on 2026-10-18. -->

**What's new against `2026-10-markov-baseline.md`:** a transition model with covariates (`forecast/logit.py`), a multinomial logistic regression fitted per horizon. Besides the current state it uses the V-Dem democracy score, log GDP per capita and its 3-year growth (Maddison 2023), log infant mortality (World Bank, from 1960), time spent in the current state, and conflict years in the last decade.

**Data:** V-Dem v16, UCDP/PRIO 26.1, Maddison Project 2023, World Bank WDI (SP.DYN.IMRT.IN).
**States and method:** as in the Markov baseline: cutoffs 1960–2014, training on what was known before each cutoff, forecasts 1 and 5 years ahead.

**Result:** the covariate model beats the Markov chain at both horizons, by about 4% on the Brier score and 10% on the log score at 1 year, and about 11% on both at 5 years. The extra conditions carry real signal beyond the current state.

**Caveats:**
- V-Dem scores and the World Bank and Maddison series are today's revised versions, not what was published at the time, so this is kinder than a true real-time test.
- No neighbour effects, ethnic exclusion or coups yet. Ethnic Power Relations and Powell & Thyne are blocked on licences.
- One model, one set of thresholds. The comparison is the point, not the absolute numbers.

Lower is better. A model is only useful if it beats both baselines.

## Calibration of the Markov model, 1 year ahead

When the model said about p, how often did it happen?

- **civil-war:** said 1% → happened 1% (n=8581), said 71% → happened 70% (n=416)
- **armed-conflict:** said 3% → happened 4% (n=7847), said 22% → happened 30% (n=77), said 68% → happened 69% (n=1073)
- **democracy:** said 1% → happened 2% (n=6098), said 97% → happened 97% (n=2899)
- **autocracy:** said 4% → happened 3% (n=3664), said 23% → happened 18% (n=724), said 95% → happened 93% (n=4609)
